  "text": "The first frost came on a Thursday. By morning, the grass had turned silver, and Mara could see the two garden sticks from her kitchen window. She had meant to bring them in, but each day there had been something else to do.

On Sunday, her brother called to ask how the green tomatoes were keeping. She told him that most were still firm. Two had ripened on the sill, and she had eaten them with salt. He said their father used to put the last ones in a drawer with an apple, though he could not remember whether it helped.

Mara tried it anyway. She found an apple at the bottom of the fruit bowl and made room for it among the wrapped tomatoes. The drawer smelled faintly of newspaper whenever she opened it.

In December, her brother came by with a small envelope. Inside were seeds he had found in the back of their father’s desk. The paper was brittle and marked only with a year. They sat at the table and tipped the seeds into Mara’s palm. Some were flat and pale; others were no bigger than dust.

‘We could plant a few,’ her brother said.

Mara folded the envelope shut. She put it beside the jar, which she had washed and kept on the shelf above the stove. Outside, the garden was covered in leaves. The sticks were still there, dark now from the rain.

Before her brother left, they went out together and pulled them from the ground. Mara wiped the mud from their ends and leaned them against the shed."
